P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, freely. Mexico has no foreign-exchange controls: no controls on transferring US dollars into or out of Mexico, the peso is freely convertible and repatriation is unrestricted. There is no surrender or repatriation requirement on export income. Anti-money-laundering rules cap CASH dollar deposits at banks (e.g. USD 4,000/month for account holders) but do not affect electronic transfers.

sources.quote: Foreign Exchange Controls There are no controls on the transfer of U.S.

sources.quote: According to the regulation, banks must observe the following limits: Account holders can deposit no more than USD 4,000 per month.

P1_fx_receipts.notes: trade.gov is a foreign (US) government source, counted as secondary for Mexico. Banxico has no 'no exchange controls' statement page that was found; Banxico's Circular 3/2012 governs FX deposit accounts (P2).

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Restricted. Under Banxico Circular 3/2012 art. 46, Mexican banks may take US-dollar demand deposits only from (a) individuals domiciled within 20 km of the US border or in Baja California or Baja California Sur, (b) companies domiciled in Mexico, and (c) foreign official missions, which must document their eligibility. Most individuals elsewhere receive foreign payments converted into an MXN account (CLABE), or keep balances in a platform (PayPal, Payoneer), or form a company to hold a USD account.

sources.quote: Institutions may receive Deposits in Foreign Currency from the following persons: I. Demand Deposits, with or without checkbook, payable in the Mexican Republic: a) From individuals who have their domicile in the strip going along twenty kilometers from the border of the United States of America, or in the states of Baja California and Baja California Sur; b) From corporate entities that have their domicile in Mexican territory

P2_fcy_account.notes: The English translation's version date was not confirmed; Banxico Circular 11/2026 amended arts. 8 and 14 (MXN accounts). Art. 46 not reported as changed. Re-check the Spanish compiled text.

P4_paypal.question: Can residents receive money via PayPal?
P4_paypal.answer: Yes. PayPal Mexico (contract with Operadora PayPal de México) is for Mexican-resident individuals aged 18+ and Mexican entities. All accounts can send and receive payments, and business accounts are recommended for selling. The standard fee for receiving domestic commercial transactions is 3.95% plus a fixed fee, plus 0.50% for senders outside Mexico. Standard withdrawal to a bank account from a Business account is free (no currency conversion); instant transfer costs MXN 40.

P5_payoneer_wise.question: Payoneer / Wise availability for residents
P5_payoneer_wise.answer: Payoneer: used in Mexico to receive USD, EUR or GBP from platforms and clients and withdraw in pesos via SPEI to Mexican banks (2–5 business days). Two independent Mexican guides recommend it for collecting from abroad, not as a savings account. Wise: Mexico is NOT on Wise's list of countries whose residents can hold money.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: No separate company is needed. An individual operates as a 'persona física' registered in the SAT's RFC under business and professional activities, or under RESICO (L3). Individuals aged 18+ with a CURP can register online. Payment providers (e.g. Stripe) onboard individuals as 'Persona Física con Actividad Empresarial'. A company (S.A. or S. de R.L.) is optional, e.g. to hold a USD account (P2).

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The RFC (Registro Federal de Contribuyentes). Personal RFCs are 13 characters. L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents are taxed on worldwide income regardless of nationality. Residence is a home in Mexico, or the centre of vital interests if there is a home abroad too (more than 50% of income from Mexico or main professional activity in Mexico). The 2026 progressive rates run from 1.92% to 35% (top bracket above MXN 5,107,703.93). RESICO (Régimen Simplificado de Confianza): individuals with business or professional activities and annual invoiced income under MXN 3.5m pay ISR of 1%–2.5% of collected income, with no deductions and a pre-filled annual return. RESICO remains in force in 2026.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: The general IVA rate is 16%. 0% applies to goods exports and to certain services 'used abroad' (LIVA art. 29-IV). That list is LIMITATIVE: technical assistance and related technical services, maquila, advertising, commissions and mediation, insurance, financing, filming or recording, call centres for calls from abroad, and IT services. The IT category has strict conditions: infrastructure and staff in Mexico, recipient IPs abroad, payment from foreign accounts. Services outside the list are subject to 16% IVA even with a foreign client. There is no small-business IVA exemption for registered individuals in general.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The new Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (LFPDPPP) was published in the DOF on 20 Mar 2025 and has been in force since 21 Mar 2025. It keeps the privacy notice (aviso de privacidad) and consent regime. New consent is required for purposes beyond the original notice (no more 'compatible purposes'), and transfers need consent unless an exception applies. INAI was abolished: the Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno is now the private-sector data authority.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: LFPC art. 56: the contract is perfected 5 business days after delivery of the good or signature of the contract, whichever is later. During that period the consumer may revoke consent without liability, and the supplier refunds the price (freight and insurance at the consumer's cost). PROFECO and media apply this cooling-off period to internet purchases.

sources.title: LFPC Artículo 56
sources.quote: ARTÍCULO 56 .- El contrato se perfeccionará a los cinco días hábiles contados a partir de la entrega del bien o de la firma del contrato, lo último que suceda.

sources.title: LFPC Artículo 56
sources.quote: Durante ese lapso, el consumidor tendrá el derecho de revocar su consentimiento sin responsabilidad alguna.

sources.title: ¿Puedo cancelar mi compra por internet después de haber recibido el producto?
sources.quote: Después de realizar una compra por internet, de acuerdo con el Artículo 56 de la LFPC, la persona podrá desistir de la compra sin responsabilidad durante los próximos 5 días hábiles contados a partir de la entrega del bien, de la firma del contrato o lo último que suceda.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.notes: Whether art. 56 (part of the door-to-door / off-premises chapter) applies to all e-commerce is an interpretation reported by media citing Profeco; the LFPC e-commerce chapter (arts. 76 bis) was not read.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: (1) RESICO: 1%–2.5% ISR on collected income for individuals under MXN 3.5m/yr, with no deductions and simplified compliance. (2) 0% IVA on qualifying exported services (LIVA art. 29-IV list). (3) No exchange controls: earnings move freely. (4) Free online RFC registration with CURP. No digital-specific tax holiday for individuals was verified.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Physical or digital goods on Etsy (Etsy seller payments are available here). (6) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Receive and withdraw'). (7) Stripe accepts merchants here, so you can take card payments directly on your own site. (8) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
